MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 15, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:02 p.m., on April 15, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 10, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ury
  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

  CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of
  City Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

  CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation. (P(1) of Subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9) Name of Case: NPDES Unfunded Mandate Claim; MS4
  Regional Permit; State Water Resources Control Board (defendant).
City Council Minutes  1  April 15, 2013
 RECESS

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with four Council Members present (Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
was absent.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for item CS2, the Council authorized staff to join the
City and Countywide joint defense agreement for the NPDES Unfunded Mandate Claim. For
item CS1, the Council provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

  P1. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Reardon presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter"
  Corporal Matthew O. Ezell and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant
  Thomas M. Reed.

  P2. Presentation by the Church of Latter Day Saints on Their Emergency
  Preparedness Academy

  The City Council received the presentation from Tom Glazier and Danny Kirkham.

  P3. Presentation by CUSD Board Member Lynn Hatton on new Programs at
  Mission Viejo Schools

  The City Council received the presentation from CUSD Board Member Lynn Hatton
  promoting Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following discussed the upcoming Arts Alive Festival on May 4 and 5, 2013, and
encouraged the Council and residents to attend: Dru Maurer, M.V.; Kent Baker, CVHS art
teacher, M.V.; Renee Keady, artist, M.V.; Sydney Atwood, artist, M.V.; Jessica Mallonee,
student artist, M.V.; Ramie Yamaguchi, student artist, M.V.; Jeremy Hoare, student artist, San
Clemente.

Bob Hayes, M.V.: invited the Council and residents to attend the April character movie, The
Tuskegee Airmen, on Sunday, April 21, 2013, at 2:00 p.m. in the City Council Chamber.

Ross Chun, Aliso Viejo: announced that Newhart Middle School will host an Earth Day Festival
on Friday, April 19, 2013, from 5:00 to 7:30 p.m. and provided the Council with an update on
Savannah's Organic Garden.

City Council Minutes  2  April 15, 2013
 Theresa Franzee, M.V.: offered details on Newhart Middle School's Earth Day Festival and
invited the Council and community to attend.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V. discussed the education system in China and stated that the United
States is very far behind. Mr. Wontrobski also expressed concern that contract cities will be
liable if OCFA has financial troubles in the future.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 5, 10, 13, 15, 16 and 17 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for regular City Council meeting of April 1, 2013, as presented.

4.  Check Register Dated March 29, 2013 in the Amount of $1,012,436.53

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Jeronimo Road Pavement Rehabilitation, Los Alisos Boulevard to Arbolitos Road &
  Peter A. Hartman Way Sidewalk Construction (CIP 837)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to R. J. Noble Company in the
  amount of $1,476,115.

7.  Annual Routine Maintenance Program for Sidewalk Grinding

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract with BPR Inc., for the period July
  1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract amount by an amount not to exceed
  $100,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to BPR Inc., for the period

City Council Minutes  3  April 15, 2013
   July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in an amount not to exceed $50,000.00.

8.  Annual Park and Facility Hardscape Construction Improvements

  (1) Approved Third Amendment to the existing contract with S. Parker Engineering Inc.,
  for the period of July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, in the amount of $ 110,000.00; and
  (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to S. Parker Engineering Inc., for the period of
  July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in an amount not to exceed $55,000.00.

9.  Annual Road and Flood Control Maintenance Contract

  (1) Approved County Agreement D-13-007 with the County of Orange for the period July
  1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, in the amount of $1,975,224.00; and (2) authorized
  issuance of a purchase order to the County of Orange for the period of July 1, 2013,
  through June 30, 2014, in an amount not to exceed $987,612.00.

11. City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2013

  Received and filed.

12. Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for February 2013

  Received and filed.

14. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for February 2013

  Received and filed.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

  18. Modifications to Policies for Sales at The Ridge - Affordable Housing Program
  and Eligibility Requirements

  Special Counsel Celeste Brady presented the staff report and summarized the
  proposed changes to the affordable housing program eligibility requirements.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  direct the MVHA Executive Director to coordinate and implement modified policies
  for sales at The Ridge - Affordable Housing Program and Eligibility Requirements.

City Council Minutes  4  April 15, 2013
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Kelley

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

  3.  Check Register Dated March 22, 2013 in the Amount of $846,660.40

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about payments made to Bravo Sign & Design,
  Getty Images/Thinkstock, and Spectrum Care Landscape for maintenance of various
  facilities.

  Staff responded with the following explanations: the City is working to help develop
  a concept for new signs at the Crown Commerce Center and the work done by Bravo
  Sign & Design will be part of the City's contribution towards that new sign
  program. Getty Images/Thinkstock is a subscription for four members of staff to
  download and use stock photography, where necessary, in the City's printed
  publications, website and blog. Lastly, staff noted that maintenance of the various
  facilities, as listed on the check register, are included in the City's standard contract
  areas but they are simply listed in greater detail on the billings and check register.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Leckness,
  to ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

  5.  Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year 2013-2014 Detailing City’s Proposed
  Use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds

  Council Member Schlicht disagreed with the eighth bullet point and stated that
  residents are not opposed to affordable housing but rather high-density housing.

  Mike Linares, CDBG Consultant, noted that staff can modify that bullet point to
  reflect the Council's desire.

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to make the amendment as described
  by Council Member Schlicht.

  Council Member Schlicht, referring to a map in the agenda report, asked how the low
  and moderate classifications are determined.

City Council Minutes  5  April 15, 2013
   Mr. Linares responded that it is based on data provided by HUD where a majority of
  residents in those areas would meet the current definition of low or moderate-income
  households. He further stated that those areas have remained the same for quite a
  few years.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Leckness,
  to adopt Resolution 13-25, as amended, Approving the City's Draft Annual Action
  Plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2013-2014 Detailing City's Proposed Use of Community
  Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds and Authorizing Submission of Such
  Plans to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

  10. Annual Maintenance Program for the Removal and Replacement of Concrete
  Sidewalks, Curbs, Gutters, Driveway Approaches, and Cross-Gutters

  Council Member Schlicht asked Director Rattay to describe the original bid amount
  verses the contract amount.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay stated that the
  $680,000 was for a two-year contract and although the budget amount was higher
  than the bid, these contracts are based on the amount that was budgeted. He further
  stated that there is usually more work to be done than money available.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to (1)
  approve First Amendment to the existing contract with S. Parker Engineering Inc.,
  for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract amount by
  an amount not to exceed $680,000.00; and (2) authorize staff to issue a purchase
  order to S. Parker Engineering Inc., for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30,
  2014, in an amount not to exceed $340,000.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

  13. Mission Viejo housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  February 2013

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she feels there was an unlawful transfer of $4.8

City Council Minutes  6  April 15, 2013
   million from this Housing Authority fund to Watermarke. She expressed concern
  that when Watermarke returned the money, it never came back to the Housing
  Authority and the City is now $4.8 million short in the general fund.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas stated that Council Member
  Schlicht's description is not accurate. Initially, when the City paid Watermarke, there
  was a $4.8 million transfer from the Housing Authority. At the same time,
  Watermarke paid the City $4.8 million for park fees and that money went into the
  park development fee fund which is separate from the general fund. The funds,
  however, are pooled together into one checking account. When the City paid the
  County, the money came from the general checking account but specifically from the
  park development fee fund. When Watermarke pulls building permits the $4.8
  million will go back to the park development fee fund.

  Council Member Schlicht noted that she still feels the money paid to the County
  should have come from the Housing Authority.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Leckness,
  to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

  *Items 15 and 17 were considered together.

  15. Annual Maintenance Program for the Removal and Replacement of Asphalt
  Pavement and Related Services

  Council Member Schlicht stated that her question addresses items 15 and 17 together
  since they are agreements for the same contract but with different contractors. She
  asked how often the City's parking lots and trails are slurried.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that most
  of the funds in the facility replacement reserve are for the trails which are slurried on
  an as-needed basis. He noted that they are typically done every seven or eight years
  and as funds are available.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  approve First Amendment to the existing contract with Ben's Asphalt Inc., for the
  period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract amount by an
  amount not-to-exceed $397,400.00; and (2) authorize staff to issue a purchase order
  to Ben's Asphalt Inc., for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in an
  amount not to exceed $198,700.00.

City Council Minutes  7  April 15, 2013
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

  17. Annual Maintenance Program for the Removal and Replacement of Asphalt
  Pavement and Related Services

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury to (1)
  approve First Amendment to the existing contract with Hardy & Harper, Inc., for the
  period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract amount by an
  amount not to exceed $ 598,600.00, and (2) authorize staff to issue a purchase order
  to Hardy & Harper, Inc., for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in an
  amount not to exceed $ 299,300.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

  16. Professional Services Agreement for Affordable Housing Consulting and
  Technical Services

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and asked the Council to amend
  the agreement and approve it, subject to the removal of the City as a party.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to approve the
  agreement among Keyser Marston Associates, Inc., the City, MVHA, and the
  Successor Agency for the Term May 1, 2013, through April 30, 2015, in an amount
  not to exceed $100,000, with the removal of the City as a party.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

  19. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

  20. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

City Council Minutes  8  April 15, 2013
   Mayor Reardon presented the report.

  21. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Attorney’s Report

  22. Amendments to the League of California Cities Bylaws

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  adopt Resolution 13-26 Approving Proposed Amendments to the League's Bylaws to
  provide that (1) resolutions submitted to the League for presentation to the General
  Assembly must include documentation that at least five or more cities, or city
  officials from at least five or more cities, have concurred in the resolution; and (2)
  the League Board may take a position on a statewide ballot measure by a 2/3rd vote
  of the Directors present.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

  23. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness noted that the Orange County Register now requires an individual to
subscribe in order to read news articles on-line. He also outlined his attendance at the Tee it Up
Fore Marines golf tournament. Council Member Leckness stated that he had a great time and he
enjoyed driving Mayor Reardon around on a golf cart.

City Council Minutes  9  April 15, 2013
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that our hearts are heavy with the news out of Boston and our
prayers are with those who suffered losses and injury. She said she can't believe that there are
people out there with the intent to kill and harm and she hopes there is swift justice.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury concurred with Council Member Schlicht that justice for the Boston
Marathon bombers should be swift and firmer than it has been in the past.

24. Bocce Ball at The Murray Center

  Council Member Ury presented his report.

  Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: expressed support for a bocce ball court at the Murray Community
  and Senior Center and stated that Casta del Sol residents would love to use it for
  tournaments.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to direct
  staff to research the cost and location for bocce ball courts a the Murray Center.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon agreed that the Marine golf tournament was excellent and she acknowledged the
many generous sponsors. She announced that Camp Pendleton's golf course is now open to the
public and she will share her coupons for a round of golf, including the cart, for $30.00 per
person. Mayor Reardon recommended that her colleagues and residents visit the Arts Alive
festival and/or the sneak peek event at Kaleidoscope. She also announced upcoming events
including the Latter Day Saints Emergency Preparedness Academy on May 4, Arts Alive on
May 4 and 5, the Earth Day Festival at Newhart School on April 19, and a National Day of
Prayer ceremony on May 2. Mayor Reardon invited Deputy Ehren Weidenkeller to the podium
and she reviewed his work history and announced that he will be leaving Mission Viejo for a
new position with the Sheriff's Department. The City Council Members thanked Deputy
Weidenkeller and wished him well in his future endeavors.

City Council Minutes  10  April 15, 2013
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:44 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting in honor of the victims and the families of the Boston
Marathon bombings, to Monday, May 6, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 6, 2013

City Council Minutes  11  April 15, 2013
